ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, officers and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Kingdom sanctions list, and FINTRAC guidance; enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) including immediate family and close associates; screening results must be timestamped, retained for five years, and refreshed immediately before the incorporation filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (via authorized service providers and NUANS name search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French, or a combination of both, using Latin script; non-Latin scripts require an approved transliteration. Each name must consist of a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element. Legal endings are limited to Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, Ltd., Corp., Inc., Limitée/LLC (as applicable). Names must not conjoin 'Alberta' or 'Canada' unless the entity is genuinely an Alberta or Canadian entity and the name otherwise complies with section 11 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be appealed by filing a written reconsideration request with the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection decision. The request must include the original NUANS report, the proposed name, and supporting arguments or third-party consents. A new submission with an amended name and payment of the prescribed fee may be filed immediately. Judicial review of a final administrative refusal may be commenced in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within six months of the decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk trading card publishing company, provided the virtual office maintains a full physical street address in Alberta, accepts service of process during normal business hours, and does not act solely as a mailbox without registered office function. Compliance with section 104 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, at less than 2% per annum in the absence of a trigger event, given the designated low-risk AML/CFT tier and the absence of any statutory licensing requirement for the business activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 5-8 on incorporation and articles, sections 102-104 on directors and officers, and section 106 on organizational proceedings
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, administered by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed Alberta Corporate Registry form, filed through an authorized Alberta registry agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required. Shares may be issued for consideration determined by the directors, subject to the Business Corporations Act. Alberta does not require a statutory escrow account for incorporation capital; any bank account and capital funding arrangements are established separately by the corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act are approved and adopted. The Corporation shall issue the authorized common shares to the subscriber for the agreed consideration, receipt of which is acknowledged. The registered office and records office shall be maintained at the addresses stated in the incorporation filing, or as subsequently approved by the Board. The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until replacement or resignation. Any director or officer is authorized to complete banking, tax, licensing, and administrative actions required to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select the Incorporation Route and Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent; federal alternative: Corporations Canada online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the company will be incorporated under the Alberta Business Corporations Act or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act. For an Alberta corporation, conduct an Alberta name search and reserve or obtain an NUANS-style name report where required by the registry agent. Ensure the proposed name is distinctive, not misleading, and includes an approved legal element such as Inc., Incorporated, Corp., or Corporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and business description
Alberta name search or registry agent name approval documentation
Registered office and records office addresses in Alberta
Director names, addresses, and consent information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, obtain the registry's reason, revise the name, and resubmit. If the registry agent identifies an incomplete search or conflict, obtain a corrected report or use a numbered corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Alberta registry agent and Alberta Corporate Registry filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate name, share classes, rights and restrictions, number of directors or director range, restrictions on share transfers if applicable, and registered office information. Confirm that at least one director is appointed and that director eligibility requirements are satisfied. Obtain incorporator signatures and any required consents.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficiencies identified by the registry agent, including missing signatures, invalid share provisions, incomplete addresses, or director eligibility issues. Resubmit the corrected articles and preserve the rejected version for the corporate file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Pay the Government Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Articles of Incorporation and supporting information through the registry agent. Pay the prescribed Alberta filing fee, together with any registry-agent service fee and optional expedited-service charge. Notarization is generally not required for standard Alberta incorporation filings unless a particular supporting document or registry-agent process requires it.
required_dossiers: Government filing fee and service-fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, obtain the written deficiency notice, correct the affected information, and resubmit through the same registry agent. If the issue concerns a name, file a numbered corporation or provide an alternative approved name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the Certificate and Establish the Corporate Record
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and the corporation's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, filed Articles, corporate access number, and registry receipt. Create the minute book, register of shareholders, securities register, director register, and register of transfers. Issue shares only after the Board approves the subscription and consideration. Record the registered office, records office, directors, officers, and beneficial ownership information in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Share certificate or electronic issuance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documents contain an error, request a corrected certificate or file the applicable amendment or correction with Alberta Corporate Registry. If a share issuance was not properly authorized, ratify it by Board resolution and update the securities register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Tax, Banking, and Governance Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Corporate Registry, financial institution, and applicable municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first Board resolutions, open the corporate bank account, obtain a CRA business number, and register for GST/HST where required or commercially appropriate. Register payroll accounts before employing staff. Obtain municipal business licensing, land-use approval, and signage or occupancy approvals for the premises. Implement annual return, corporate-record, tax, and beneficial-ownership compliance calendars.
required_dossiers: Bank account mandate and signing authorities
Municipal business licence and zoning documentation
Payroll and GST/HST registration information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or municipal application is delayed, respond to the authority's information request, correct the application, and obtain written confirmation of registration. If a municipal use is not permitted, amend the premises, obtain a development or occupancy approval, or relocate the operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade; municipal licensing and planning authorities administer premises-specific approvals
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general Alberta manufacturing licence is ordinarily required for collectible trading-card printing. Municipal business licence, zoning approval, development permit, occupancy approval, and building or electrical permits may be required depending on the premises and equipment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-specific environmental impact assessment for ordinary commercial printing; project-specific review or approvals may apply to significant expansions, regulated emissions, hazardous materials, or designated activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act requirements, applicable approvals or registrations, municipal sewer bylaws, hazardous-waste rules, and air-emission requirements. Manage inks, solvents, coatings, foils, waste paper, and contaminated containers as required. Obtain authorization before any regulated wastewater discharge or material air release; maintain records for waste manifests, storage, spill response, and emissions controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal building, development, occupancy, electrical, and fire-code approvals where applicable. Maintain fire detection, extinguishing, emergency-exit, storage, and evacuation systems in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code. Comply with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation, including hazard assessments, worker training, machine guarding, chemical labeling and safety data sheets, personal protective equipment, ventilation, incident reporting, and workplace inspections. Structural load review is required where printing presses, paper stock, racking, or other heavy equipment may affect floor capacity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada); business registration and GST/HST administration conducted through the CRA My Business Account portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from the Canada Revenue Agency, generally by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number). If taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, the entity must also open a GST/HST program account (suffix RT). Non-resident applicants may submit Form RC1 by mail or fax and must provide registered corporate details, Canadian contact/legal address, and information on the business activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer subject to Part I corporate income tax; it is not a pass-through entity. Alberta provincial corporate income tax is levied on allocable taxable income in addition to federal corporate tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a US-style check-the-box election; corporate entity-level taxation is mandatory for incorporated entities. Relevant statutory elections include the GST/HST election for closely related corporations to treat certain intercorporate supplies as nil-rated or to file a combined registration under ETA s. 273, a section 216 election for a non-resident to report Canadian rental and timber income, and provincial/federal corporate tax allocation procedures under applicable tax collection agreements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST). Alberta does not impose a provincial retail sales tax; only the federal GST at 5% applies on taxable supplies made in Alberta, unless the supply zero-rating or exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. A person becomes a mandatory GST/HST registrant when taxable supplies made in Canada, including those of associated persons, exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the previous four consecutive calendar quarters. Alberta has no separate PST registration threshold because no provincial sales tax applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada currently imposes no national real-time electronic invoicing, continuous transaction control, or digital fiscal stamping mandate. Registered suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST information and retain records; GST/HST returns generally must be filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or by an authorized representative through CRA's online services. There is no mandatory government API clearance for invoice issuance, but CRA provides Represent a Client APIs and digital account administration for compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of tangible personal property qualifies for zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act where the supplier exports the goods directly or delivers them to a common carrier or consignee for export as part of the supply, and the goods leave Canada within a reasonable period (administratively expected within 60 days). Offshore services may be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and the service is not in connection with real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or a Canadian resident receiving the service. Export zero-rating requires that the goods or services are substantiated by contemporaneous export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Customs Export Declaration or approved electronic export report (Form B13A)
Bill of Lading or air waybill clearly evidencing destination outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank foreign-exchange remittance evidence showing payment by the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess an export supply to charge uncollected GST if the required export documentation is incomplete or the foreign consideration is not repatriated within a reasonable period. A zero-rating claim found to be unsupported attracts the full 5% GST on the selling price, interest, and administrative penalties. Knowingly making a false statement or omitting material information can give rise to penalties under ETA s. 285 of up to 25% of the net tax sought to be avoided, and wilful evasion may result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. GST/HST registrants must retain export records for at least six years from the end of the taxation year to which the records relate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and systemic liquidity authority; the Exchange Rate and Funds Management function is executed by the Department of Finance Canada; foreign-exchange trade surveillance and cross-border transfer reporting are administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account; no exchange-control approval, central-bank permit, or repatriation licence is required for dividends, management fees, interest, royalties, or loan repayments. Canada operates a free-floating exchange-rate regime. Profit repatriation from an Alberta business corporation is legally unrestricted, subject only to (i) corporate solvency and balance-sheet tests under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), (ii) directors' due-diligence duties, and (iii) withholding-tax compliance on non-resident distributions. The Investment Canada Act applies to acquisitions of control of Canadian businesses, not to ongoing current-account flows, and is not engaged by ordinary inbound capital injections into a wholly owned trading-card printing entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Canada. CAD/USD export receipts may be held freely in foreign-currency accounts maintained with any authorized Schedule I bank. Mandatory requirements are limited to (i) record-keeping for cross-border wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC reporting, (ii) transfer-pricing documentation under Section 247 of the Income Tax Act for intercompany payments, and (iii) bank-account signatory and boarding rules under the banks' AML compliance programs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD dual-currency with global FX workstation)
Operational Account (CAD clearing plus USD sweep and merchant settlement)
Operational Account with integrated trade-finance and documentary collection desk
Operational Account (CAD and USD clearing rails, plus supply-chain finance)
Operational Account (regional presence; lower priority for Alberta-based cross-border operations)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (conditional). Canadian-regulated fintech payment providers such as Stripe (global payments), Authorize.Net (card acquiring), Nuvei, and Wise Business (cross-border EMI-style settlement) are legally usable for collecting card-sale revenue and paying international suppliers; however, none can serve as the primary liquidity house for the Alberta entity. Legal constraints: (i) offshore digital EMIs hold non-Canadian e-money licences and are not deemed authorized deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act; they cannot originate or receive Lynx-wire finality in CAD; (ii) under the Retail Payment Activities Act (2021, in force), payment service providers must register with the Bank of Canada and maintain settlement arrangements with a Payments Canada participant; (iii) all CAD clearing must visibly terminate at a Schedule I bank account held in the entity's own name to preserve tax-basis traceability and audit comfort. Recommended architecture: Schedule I bank as the treasury anchor; Stripe/Authorize.Net as front-end card rails; Wise or a foreign-exchange broker as a secondary, low-value remittance corridor only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under FINTRAC's AML/KYC framework where the director/officer completes video-verified identity proofing and the corporate pack is certified by an authorized signatory; however, all Schedule I banks in practice require an in-person or video interview with at least one director or officer holding a Canadian nexus (residential address or registered office authority). No statutory mandate requires a physical appearance in Alberta, but a physical or notarized appearance materially shortens the high-risk non-resident review. Recommended execution: (i) appoint a Canadian-resident director or corporate officer prior to account opening; (ii) attend one in-person meeting in Calgary or Edmonton with the treasury relationship officer; (iii) serve the bank with the registered office address and the corporate records book at the entity's Alberta registered address; (iv) provide two authorized signing directors with dual-signature authority above CAD 10,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with foreign passport and no Canadian credit or residency footprint; automatic enhanced due diligence (EDD) referral if UBO tax residency is in a FATF-monitored jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Notarized passport copy of each UBO; (ii) global beneficial-ownership chart signed by a director; (iii) 12-month bank statement from the foreign parent demonstrating lawful source of funds for the capital injection; (iv) certified business-licence slide from the ultimate parent's jurisdiction; (v) reference letter from the existing foreign relationship bank; (vi) Alberta Corporate Registry certificate and initial annual return confirming the registered address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial paper trail for high-frequency, high-volume inbound deposits associated with e-commerce sales of collectible trading cards; AML ruleplaces classify payment aggregation as higher risk if merchant and cardholders are not identifiable.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Signed and dated distribution agreements with large retailers (Walmart, Target Canada e-commerce partners) and marketplace agreements; (ii) pro forma invoices and order-confirmation screenshots; (iii) card-printing and finishing contracts with security holographic foil suppliers; (iv) customs and freight-forwarder bills of lading matching shipment value; (v) a written cash-flow narrative signed by the CFO classifying each card line as Low_Risk_Standard under the entity's own risk-tier policy; (vi) monthly merchant-settlement statements from Stripe and Authorize.Net reconciled to bank deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal inbound capital injection registered as a shareholder loan rather than share subscription, creating a debt-to-equity ratio outside the bank's comfort band and potential treaty-relevant interest payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Notarized shareholder loan agreement setting a fixed interest rate aligned with arm's-length terms; (ii) board resolution authorizing the borrowing and the pledge of the Canadian entity's receivables; (iii) source-of-funds evidence from the lender (6-month bank statements); (iv) contemporaneous CBCA/ABCA solvency certificate confirming the loan does not defeat corporate solvency; (v) tax-comfort letter from a Canadian cross-border tax advisor confirming that interest withholding under Part XIII will be satisfied and that the loan does not constitute a prohibited benefit under the Income Tax Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Signature-mandate red flag where the sole signing director is a non-resident or where all signatories are from the same foreign parent, raising operational and fraud-nexus concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certified copy of the board resolution appointing a Canadian-resident treasury officer as co-signatory; (ii) certificate of incumbency from the corporate secretary listing specimen signatures; (iii) two-factor authorization protocol (approving officer plus executing officer); (iv) background cheques (enhanced individual profile) for each signatory; (v) bank-provided fraud-warning questionnaire completed and acknowledged; (vi) undertaking to provide quarterly financial statements and updated UBO declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity or shareholder-loan proceeds as a SWIFT MT103 from the parent company's bank to the Alberta operating account at the named Schedule I bank. Use Canada's Balance-of-Payments purpose code CAN-G1 ('General remittance and investment') with a beneficiary reference string containing the share-subscription agreement number or the board-resolution date. For amounts above CAD 10,000, the receiving bank files a FINTRAC Large Cash/Electron Funds Transfer Report (EFTR). Required verification bundle: (i) board resolution of the Canadian entity authorizing the specific account and purpose; (ii) certified copy of the ultimate-parent board resolution; (iii) executed share-subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement; (iv) the sending bank's SWIFT confirmation; (v) a tax organizer entry cross-referencing the injection to the CBCA share register or to the short-term intercompany note. There is no central-bank approval step; however, funds originating from a non-Canadian bank in a foreign currency will be converted to CAD at the receiving bank's spot rate unless a dedicated USD sub-account is opened in parallel.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For steelyarding production and printing costs paid to offshore suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 (international wire) for balances above CAD 10,000, and the Canadian Lynx high-value payment system (operated by Payments Canada) for same-day finality in CAD; for trade-payable security, open an irrevocable commercial documentary letter of credit (LC) with the Alberta bank as issuing bank, advised/confirmed by the beneficiary's bank, and settle via reimbursement clause through SWIFT MT202. For recurring low-value disbursements (digital platforms, cloud services, small print-vendor invoices), use Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) direct deposits or pre-authorized debits funded from the operational account. Card-acquiring proceeds from Stripe and Authorize.Net are batched daily into the CAD operating account via their partner banks. All outbound payments must carry the relevant Canadian purpose code CAN-P1 (trade settlement) and must be supported by underlying invoices, PO numbers, and the entity's transfer-pricing file where the payee is related.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forward contracts (CAD/USD) executed bilaterally with a Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a plain FX Master Agreement, no exchange-traded requirement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for CAD are market-permissible only in exotic cross-currency pairs where local delivery is impractical; standard CAD/USD NDF is unnecessary because CAD is freely deliverable; if offered, it must be limited to tenors under 12 months and booked with a licensed Canadian derivatives dealer.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD-USD, CAD-EUR) for converting parent-funded floating-rate loans into fixed-rate synthetic CAD debt, supported by the entity's prudent-practice treasury policy.
European-style over-the-counter FX options (vanilla puts/calls) purchased (not written) to protect the collectible-card export margin, with premiums expensed through the treasury line.
Exchange-traded FX futures and options on USD/CAD listed on the Montreal Exchange (MX) for highly liquid, short-dated hedging tranches.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry) – mandatory declaration of directors, registered office, and share structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the incorporation/registration anniversary (e.g., anniversary July 15 → due September 13)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an additional CAD 50 fee (total CAD 100); failure to file for one year permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation; reinstatement requires payment of arrears plus a CAD 100 restoration application fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (combined federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax filing via Schedule 5 allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); data shared with Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T2 due within 6 months after fiscal year end (e.g., December 31 year-end → June 30); balance-due day is 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs, or 3 months after year-end for CCPCs claiming the small business deduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (up to 12 months); repeat offender penalty of 10%; daily compound interest on overdue balances; directors may be personally liable for unremitted source deductions and corporate tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (GST34) – applicable where annual filing election is in place; otherwise monthly or quarterly returns apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year end for annual filers (e.g., December 31 year-end → March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 1% of the amount owing (minimum CAD 100) plus 0.25% per month up to 4 months; prescribed-rate daily compound interest; repeated non-filing can trigger CRA demand letters, garnishment, and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) record and annual board/shareholder resolutions (approval of financial statements, appointment of directors/officers, auditor waiver)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's own statutory minute book; no external registry filing required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held no later than 15 months after the previous AGM and no later than 18 months after incorporation; resolutions effective as of meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who default are liable to a fine of up to CAD 5,000; a shareholder may petition the court to compel the AGM; continuing default may be cited in administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO register) confirmation and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's own statutory records under Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) sections 114.1–114.5; available for inspection by regulatory, law enforcement, and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation at the AGM; any share transfer causing a change in significant control must be recorded within 15 days of the corporation receiving notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly failing to maintain or update the ISC register is an offence under ABCA: liable on summary conviction to a fine of up to CAD 200,000, imprisonment up to 6 months, or both.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Corporations Canada) – conditionally applicable only if the entity is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act and registered extra-provincially in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of federal incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing for one year after notice permits Corporations Canada to dissolve the federal corporation; revival requires payment of all outstanding fees plus a revival fee, and reinstatement of the Alberta extra-provincial registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), distributing (public) corporations must appoint an auditor at each AGM. A non-distributing (private) corporation may waive the auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution (ABCA s.168) and file a Notice of Waiver of Appointment of Auditor with the Alberta Corporate Registry (CAD 50 filing fee). Any shareholder or group holding at least 5% of the voting shares may demand an audit. There is no revenue/asset-size threshold under ABCA; the auditor obligation is triggered by public solicitation or shareholder demand.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may use ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises). Annual financial statements must be prepared for the AGM and must reconcile to the T2 corporation income tax return (federal and Alberta provincial portions).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's ABCA (ss. 114.1–114.5) requires every non-exempt corporation to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO register). The register identifies each individual holding 25% or more of voting shares or exercising de facto control, including the nature and date of control and any step-change events. Directors must review and confirm the register's accuracy annually at the AGM, update it within 15 days of any notified share transfer or change in significant control, and retain written confirmation in the minute book. No annual ISC filing is currently required with the Alberta Corporate Registry, but the register must be immediately available for inspection by the Alberta Securities Commission, police, and tax authorities.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% general combined rate (15.0% federal Part I + 8.0% Alberta) on taxable income; on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income eligible for the federal small business deduction only, the combined rate is reduced to 11.0% (9.0% federal + 2.0% Alberta).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal general rate reduction (13 percentage points to 15%); federal small business deduction (19 percentage points to 9%) on first CAD 500,000 active business income; Alberta small business deduction (6 percentage points to 2%); no Alberta general tax reduction; scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) 33% refundable/15% non-refundable investment tax credits; temporary 10% Canadian manufacturing and processing zero-emission technology? (not applicable); film/media credits not applicable to trading-card printing.
